The fires' own credential, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (the "coding-agent subscription token" of ruling 1), still authenticates through the fires' exact path (`claude auth status` under `~/.claude-fires` reads loggedIn; a one-word `-p` probe answered), so the value exposed on 2026-08-25 is STILL LIVE: the owner mints a new one (`claude setup-token`), pastes it as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=`, and revokes the old one in his account; the attended session re-probes and closes. The droplet holds no stray copy (`find / -name .env.local` empty, `/opt/goldrush/.env.local` absent, read-only over the deploy's own ssh path). The Codex login was refreshed today (`~/.codex/auth.json`, "Logged in using ChatGPT"). Retires when: both new values answer live to the same read-only calls, the Claude probe passes on a NEW value (`.env.local` rewritten) and the owner says the old one is revoked. The original finding is the F-2299-1 row of s2299 below. ➡️ **UPDATE 2026-09-24 18:15 local (owner: "I rotated all tokens in the .env.local file", "I rolled it again"):** the owner rotated all three at the providers and minted a new Claude Code token, but pasted twice into the sibling folder's copy (`Gold Rush-history-local/.env.local`, the pre-rewrite local history), which nothing reads; the attended session found it by mtime, verified its values read-only (Cloudflare `active`, ElevenLabs `200`, the new Claude token answers through the fires' path, per-line hashes: the three rotated lines DIFFERENT, the account id, the router key and the droplet host identical), backed the old root file up outside every git tree (`~/.goldrush/env.local.bak-2026-09-24`, mode 600; a `.bak` beside `.env.local` would NOT be gitignored) and copied the edited file into the repo root; re-verified from the root: Cloudflare `active`, ElevenLabs `200`, Claude `ok`, `wrangler whoami` logged in. Then I logged in again, logged in here, then did claude setup-token, copied it in .env.local and then told you done."):** MEASURED, not inferred: after that button, the August token (from the backup) and the 18:13 token (minted before the button) BOTH still answer through the fires' auth path; the button ends browser and CLI sessions (this CLI needed `/login`) but does not revoke long-lived `claude setup-token` tokens. 🔺 **F-2641-1 — THE GATE-CALLER BASELINE CARRIED FIVE STALE ORPHAN ENTRIES WHOSE STATED REASON WAS FALSE ON BOTH COUNTS, AND THE INHERITED CAUTION AGAINST TIGHTENING IT WAS TRUE OF A DIFFERENT TOOL (measured and cured s2641; board DRY at lock and THREE ASTRA LANES LIVE at handoff; CODEX-WALL standing, owner POLICY, read AT SOURCE).** `gate-caller-audit` has closed with *"5 baselined orphan(s) now have a caller — tighten the baseline"* for several fires, and s2640 carried it forward as PRE-EXISTING and UNCLAIMED with a stated reason: *"tightening a baseline is a deliberate act, never a drive-by, for exactly F-2595-1’s wholesale-blessing reason."* 🔑 **THAT REASON IS TRUE OF `law-pointer-guard --update` AND MEASURABLY FALSE OF THIS TOOL, established BY READING rather than by running: `gate-caller-audit.mjs:480–498` carries the s2199 cure (F-2199-2) written for exactly that hazard — an entry that gains a caller MOVES to `superseded` (*"out of the ratchet, still on disk, still greppable … This is history, not amnesty"*) instead of being deleted, and `batterySteps` is ADDITIVE and never rebuilt (F-2201-1, `:493–498`). Two baselines, two `--update` arms, OPPOSITE safety properties — and the warning written for one was carried onto the other.** That is the §2.0b lesson on a ledger file: **a predecessor’s stated reason for declining is a CLAIM WITH A PRICE ON IT, not a constraint; re-measure it before inheriting the restraint.** 📊 **MEASURED, NOT INHERITED — all five genuinely have callers: the four `review-*` tests via the npm alias `test:review-fixes`, which `test:node-guards` now CHAINS at the end of its own leg list, and `anim-pass-dupecheck.mjs` via `anim-pass-grid.test.mjs:39` (itself a rooted leg). Their baseline reason read *"NO CALLER, and DELIBERATELY UNROOTED because it is RED against this tree"* — **FALSE ON BOTH COUNTS: `npm run test:review-fixes` is `24 pass / 0 fail`, rc=0, `6.0 s`** (routed through `node`, since the `npm run test:*` form is gate-refused — F-2359-1). So F-SSL-4’s standing recommendation, *"root it with the src half, or retire it if that half never lands"*, is **DISCHARGED for those four**; `review-account-creation` and `review-terminal-views` remain grandfathered and OPEN, which is the correct residue and is stated rather than quietly folded in.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO, NOT a false green, and the audit PASSED both before and after — a stale grandfather entry does not change the verdict. What it does is make the baseline LIE to its reader: a fire consulting it would have read a live coverage hole and a red test where there is neither, which is the FALSE URGENCY class F-2566-1/F-2570-1/F-2571-1 each name on a different bucket.** ✅ **VERIFIED ON A SCRATCH COPY BEFORE LANDING (F-1274-2), with the copy asserted byte-identical first: `--update-baseline --baseline /tmp/…` then an entry-by-entry diff — `grandfathered 22 → 17`, `superseded 19 → 23`, `batterySteps 285 → 304` with **0 REMOVED**, **0 reasons changed**, **0 reasons lost** (all 22 + 19 survive VERBATIM, checked on PARSED values). **`added=0` to grandfathered is the precondition a fire MUST check before running this arm at all**: the writer grandfathers any NEW orphan with a `TODO: say why` placeholder, so on a board carrying an un-excused orphan the same command would silently EXCUSE it. Today the audit reports none, which is why it was safe today and may not be tomorrow. Verdict unchanged (`PASS`, rc=0) on both baselines; only the advisory line disappears. `gate-caller-audit.test.mjs` `45 pass / 0 fail`.** ⚠️ **ONE METHOD NOTE PAID FOR IN THIS FIRE, AND IT NEARLY BECAME A PUBLISHED FALSE ALARM: my own diff check reported **`7` reason texts LOST**, three of them belonging to entries I had never touched. **THE CHECK WAS THE BUG, NOT THE TOOL.** It tested a `.slice(0,120)` of a PARSED JSON string for membership in the RAW file bytes — where `"` is escaped as `\"` — so it fails on any reason whose first 120 characters span a quote. Re-run on PARSED values: `22 of 22` grandfathered and `19 of 19` superseded preserved, **0 lost**. **A raw-text substring test over JSON is not a control, and it fails in the ALARMING direction** — F-2606-1’s truncation lesson one ENCODING layer in, and the tell was that it accused entries my edit could not have reached.** 🚫 **NO NEW GUARD, and the restraint is measured rather than lazy: the mechanism ALREADY EXISTS and already works — the audit’s own advisory is precisely the detector, it is rooted, and it reddened on demand.
